title: Multiplication in a probabilistic program
statement:
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ natural-number registers, state set $\Lambda$, and oracle, and fix an input $x$ and register bound $B$. Let $i,j,a,b,R$ be register indices satisfying $i
e a$, $j
e b$, $j
e R$, $R
e b$, $i
e j$, $i
e R$, $R
e a$, $j
e a$, and $i
e b$. Suppose the instructions are as follows: $mo$ compares $i$ and $a$, going to $ex$ if equal and to $mo_1$ otherwise; $mo_1$ clears register $j$ and goes to $mi$; $mi$ compares $j$ and $b$, going to $mo_2$ if equal and to $mi_1$ otherwise; $mi_1$ increments $R$ and goes to $mi_2$; $mi_2$ increments $j$ and returns to $mi$; and $mo_2$ increments $i$ and returns to $mo$. For any rational $q$ and valuation $v$ bounded by $B$ with $v(i)\le v(a)$ and $v(R)+(v(a)-v(i))v(b)\le B$, assume that for every $z\le B$, the configuration at $ex$ with $R$ set to $v(R)+(v(a)-v(i))v(b)$, $i$ set to $v(a)$, and $j$ set to $z$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. Then the configuration at $mo$ with valuation $v$ has the same semantics and acceptance probability.

Every register value of $v$ is at most $B$
For every $z\le B$, the specified configuration at $ex$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$ under bound $B
